messages:
alex: Quick sync  Updated a compact filter drawer mock that collapses to an icon on narrow screens: https://www.figma.com/file/zzzzz/catalog-filter-drawer
nina: saw it. nice real estate saving. question: when collapsed, how does discoverability work for new users? maybe show a subtle pulse on first visit or a tooltip "Filters"
riya: accessibility: the drawer should trap focus when open, ESC to close, and return focus to the invoking control. also ensure each group has aria-expanded and aria-controls
tom: compare table note: when we pin a version it currently changes row order which is surprising. suggestion: keep order stable but add a pinned badge + sticky header entry for pinned rows (so pinned items are visible during scroll)
alex: good call. I prototyped a thin sticky strip above the compare table called "Pinned versions" that clones minimal row info and links back to the original row
nina: UX nit: the sticky strip should be keyboard reachable and announce itself to screen readers: "Pinned versions. 2 items pinned." with a button "Manage pinned versions"
riya: badges: performance badges currently use single-letter labels (P/T) which is cryptic. propose full short labels like "latency" or "throughput" and an icon. too many colours right now leads to legends being overwhelming
tom: can we allow badge sorting? i.e., column header drop-down to pick which badge is primary sort key for compare (latency, cost, qps)
alex: backend can expose metrics in a metadata column for sort. product question: do we want to sort by median or p99 by default? suggestion: median for discoverability, p99 under advanced sort
nina: copy tweak: badge tooltip should start with human-friendly phrase, e.g., "Median latency: 68 ms" rather than "median:68ms". add units and separators for large numbers: "12,300 qps"
riya: touch/mobile: for long chip lists in filter drawer, use a draggable handle + inertial scroll; avoid horizontal scroll for chips inside the drawer because it conflicts with page swipe gestures
tom: visual accessibility: badge contrast for small text should meet 3:1. if a badge uses an accent color, outline the text with a subtle dark shadow or use a slightly darker background for label text to meet ratio
alex: mock snippet for the new legend (compact):
```json
["latency": "90 ms median", "p99": "250 ms", "qps": "12,000"]
```
nina: love the mini-legend. also add a "?" help anchor in the catalog header that opens a small modal describing badge sources and update cadence
riya: keyboard flows: when using compare with keyboard only, hitting "c" should toggle compare mode, hitting "p" while focused on a row should toggle pin. we need to ensure these shortcuts are documented and can be disabled in prefs
tom: for pin affordance: make the pin a visible pill button with label "Pin" (icon + text) instead of an icon-only control. that reduces discoverability issues for new users
alex: agree. I'll push a patch to the component with the pill style and aria-pressed semantics
ui-ci-bot: Preview build deployed: https://ci.redwood.dev/previews/1935801234. Includes: filter-drawer, pinned-strip, badge-legend, keyboard-shortcuts overlay
nina: I'll run contrast checks + keyboard walkthrough on preview and post results here with screenshots by EOD
riya: I'll update the accessibility checklist and add items: "drawer focus trap, escape close, aria-live for pinned count, keyboard shortcuts discoverability"
alex: thanks all. next steps: nina + riya validate preview, tom to prototype badge-sort dropdown, i'll update Figma and component tokens. ping here when PR ready :thumbsup:
